testalinden2010.title: Review of the Testalinden Dam Failure
testalinden2010.container: Victoria: Province of British Columbia, Deputy Solicitor General, 13 July 2010
testalinden2010.note: Pp. 7–9: the dam’s history from 1937 and the warnings; p. 10: the hiker’s report; pp. 11–12: the breach and the response; pp. 14–15: BC’s dam safety program and the dam’s Low rating; pp. 4–5: twelve recommendations.

asdso-testalinden.authors: Association of State Dam Safety Officials
asdso-testalinden.title: Testalinden Dam (British Columbia, 2010)
asdso-testalinden.container: Case study, Lessons Learned from Dam Incidents and Failures (damfailures.org); peer-reviewed by M. Noseworthy, BC Ministry of Forests, Lands, Natural Resource Operations and Rural Development
asdso-testalinden.note: Height 2.5 m, silty sand and glacial till built with horses and a Fresno scraper, no engineering design; El. 1,810 m, about 1,500 m above the valley; about 29 acre-feet at the top of the crest; snowmelt overflow scoured through the crest (quoting Tannant 2015); mudflow at least an order of magnitude larger than the water released; losses over C$20 million; 1,132 of 1,900 registered dams assessed; Low in 2010, Significant under the regulation as amended in 2021.
